title: Python Object-Oriented Programming: Classes, Objects and Core Concepts
learningObjectives: Explain the core concepts of Python Object-Oriented Programming: Classes, Objects and Core Concepts.
Choose an appropriate object-oriented design for a small Python problem.
Trace object state and method calls accurately.
Apply Python class features with correct method and attribute behavior.
Recognize design trade-offs, edge cases and maintainability concerns.

understand.concept: Object-oriented programming organizes related state and behavior into objects. A class defines a reusable structure; each object is an instance with its own identity and state. Python supports encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism, but these are design tools rather than requirements for every program.
understand.whyItMatters: Classes help model entities with related data and operations, while small functions and simple data structures remain preferable for simpler tasks.
understand.analogy: A class is like a recipe and each object is a separately prepared dish; objects can have different values even when made from the same recipe.
understand.summary: Python Object-Oriented Programming: Classes, Objects and Core Concepts introduces a focused part of Python's object model and its practical use.

explain.narrative: Study the concept, trace the receiver and state for each operation, then run the examples. Pay attention to Python's conventions and documented protocol behavior rather than assuming that class syntax provides strict access control.

examples.title: Define a simple class
examples.explanation: A class groups behavior; calling it creates an instance.

examples.title: Create two independent objects
examples.code:
class Counter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.value = 0
a = Counter()
b = Counter()
a.value += 2
print(a.value, b.value)
examples.explanation: Each instance stores its own state.

examples.title: Inspect an object's type
examples.explanation: The type of an instance is its class.

examples.title: Attach and read instance state
Use a method to update state
examples.code:
class Score:
    def __init__(self): self.points = 0
    def add(self, amount): self.points += amount
s = Score()
s.add(5)
print(s.points)
examples.explanation: Methods can change the state belonging to their instance.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small program that demonstrates python object-oriented programming: classes, objects and core concepts. Write down the object types, relevant attributes, method calls and expected state changes before running it.
practise.independentTask: Extend the example into a small domain model of your choice. Add validation, clear method names, boundary tests and a short explanation of why your design uses classes rather than simpler functions or data structures.
hints: Identify which object owns each piece of state.
Trace the first argument supplied to every bound method.
Prefer explicit invariants and small public interfaces.
Test at least one boundary or unsupported input.
Use composition when it models the relationship more accurately than inheritance.
practise.challenge: Refactor the model into a testable design with clear responsibilities, documented public behavior and tests for normal, boundary and invalid cases.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute on the supported Python version and match their outputs.
The implementation follows Python's documented class and special-method semantics.
State changes are scoped to the intended object or class.
Unsupported inputs produce a deliberate result or a clear exception.
The design avoids unnecessary inheritance, shared mutable defaults and misleading private-access claims.
